summary: Codex found a real defect at turn 2 that I consented past twice, and I verified it at its source before accepting the repair: D-054's Subject line reads 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only', so it and D-057 could never have supplied the owner path for these condition-2 V2 deferrals. Turn 3 does not merely drop the wrong citation — it records that the owner path is blocked, names what would unblock it, separates owner-recording from the later MF-6, and adds a rejected alternative for the citation it withdrew. All eighteen digests match, the register remains untouched, and the entry still specifies no file-08 edit at all.

selfCorrection.summary: I consented at turns 1 and 2 to an entry whose clause 3 read 'Named owners still record (D-054 / D-057).' Codex's ADV-D095-T2-01 is right that those entries do not reach these rows, and the fact was one I already had.
selfCorrection.whatIDid: At both turns I tested the named attack, 'coordinator pretends to be the named owner'. The entry disclaimed it in four places — the header's 'Does not make the coordinator those owners', clause 3's own sentence, the conditional framing of every effect, and a rejected alternative — and I confirmed against the five artifacts that each names a file-08 owner distinct from the coordinator. Having satisfied myself on the disclaimer, I stopped.
selfCorrection.whatIMissed: The same clause pointed forward to D-054 and D-057 as the authority under which those owners would later record, and I never tested that pointer. D-054's Subject field states its scope in one line: 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only', and its decision grants the assistant preview-scope recordings for 'the named V1 owners' of 'preview Route B dispositions', on the reasoning that 'Those owner roles have no other human.' D-057 is mechanics under that same authority and requires a 'row Route B selection' among its preconditions. None of DR-106, DR-108, DR-109, DR-110, DR-113, DR-116 or the Windows platform set is a condition-1 row, none has a Route B selection, and their owners — security, platform, release, evidence, storage, product — are not the named V1 owners. So the entry recorded a route that does not exist, and I passed it twice.
selfCorrection.theDisciplineIFailedToApply: When an entry disclaims an authority for itself and points at a different authority for the later act, the pointer needs the same scrutiny as the disclaimer. A correct refusal plus a wrong forward reference still leaves a wrong route in the register. Put more sharply: an attack answered is not a citation checked. I had checked this entry's other citations — the D-013 / D-035 / D-042 / D-066 recording class, each verified present and of the right shape — and did not extend that to the one citation carrying authority rather than precedent.
selfCorrection.aggravating: I already knew D-054's scope from reviewing that cycle and D-057's, where the grant's confinement to the named V1 owners was the point of the amendment. This was not a fact I lacked; it was one I did not bring to bear.

Restoring the sentence costs nothing. It is a transparency regression rather than an error, so it does not warrant a fourth turn.

The attack 'ADV-D095-T2-01 not landed' fails, and I verified the underlying finding at its source rather than accepting Codex's characterisation. D-054's Subject line reads 'condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only'; its decision names 'the named V1 owners' recording 'accepted preview Route B dispositions'; D-057 is 'Mechanics of preview-scope owner recording' whose 'Authority is user-made D-054, not this entry' and whose preconditions include a 'row Route B selection'. The rows here are condition-2 V2 rows with no Route B selection and different owners, so the disposition's statement that these are 'condition-1 V1 Route-B owner machinery' which 'do not authorize owner-recording of these condition-2 deferrals' is exactly right.

The repair goes further than withdrawing the citation, which is what makes it a fix rather than a deletion. The header adds 'Does not invoke D-054 / D-057 for these rows' and extends the non-overturn list to D-057; clause 1 recasts the act as 'the coordinator recording only'; clause 3 states the owner path is 'blocked until an applicable authority and mechanics are adopted' and names both routes that would unblock it — a reviewed user amendment covering the named security, platform, release, evidence, storage, product and architecture roles, or a D-000-reviewed mechanics entry that is not D-057's V1 Route-B file — and preserves that DR-116 remains Route C; and a new rejected alternative records the withdrawn citation itself.

Blocking rather than improvising is the right outcome here. D-002 requires each deferred item to get a recorded disposition and never silence, so there is pressure to find some owner path; the entry instead records that no applicable authority exists yet. Condition 2 is NOT MET regardless, so nothing is lost by waiting, and inventing a grant would have been the more serious error.

The attack 'ADV-D095-T2-02 not landed' fails. Turn 2 read 'Owner-recording plus a later MF-6 is the C2 deferral-limb write', which ran the two acts together; turn 3 reads 'Owner-recording, when later authorized, precedes a separate later D-000-reviewed MF-6. Neither owner-recording nor MF-6 occurs in this entry', and the readiness effect makes the sequence explicit — condition 2 remains unchanged until an applicable owner recording lands and a separate later MF-6 records the disposition in file 08.

The attack 'coordinator pretends to be the named owner' fails on stronger ground than before. The rejected alternative no longer cites D-054 and D-057 as the answer — which was itself part of the defect — and now reads 'D-000 does not silently make the coordinator every security / release / evidence / platform owner.'

The attack 'edits file 08' fails by absence, re-tested: the subject contains zero fenced blocks and zero occurrences of the word Replace, so there is no edit to mis-target, and file 08 measures 45dc4611… unmodified in my working tree and matching the pin.

The attack 'retries D-094 or names G03/G04' fails: the only mention is the refusal 'D-094 is CONTESTED, not adopted. G03/G04 stay reserved. This entry does not retry D-094', with a matching rejected alternative. I re-confirmed the register is untouched by that CONTESTED cycle — the 16-of-18 fragment is present, 'PARTLY MET' appears once, 'reserved, not named' three times and 'named: harness.' sixteen times — so 'Condition 4 stays 16 of 18 PARTLY MET' is true of bytes.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all eighteen rows. The five artifact digests, my five artifact verdicts and the five Codex artifact verdicts all match, the Codex files hashed without opening; so do my two entry verdicts at 25c3119d… and b6539bd0…, both parsed to confirm the recital's 'Claude 2 CONSENT both turns' with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX each; and the Codex turn-2 verdict at 1967128d…, hashed without opening. The attacks 'marks any deferred row SATISFIED' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail: every occurrence is a refusal or a standing statement, clause 4 keeps the rows OPEN and keeps Windows off the register as a row, and the readiness effect records zero SATISFIED.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, and the substance of this turn is a correction of mine. I passed this entry twice while it cited D-054 and D-057 as the path by which the named owners would later record these deferrals. D-054 says what it covers in its own Subject line — condition 1 owner-recording for preview Route B only — and these are condition-2 V2 rows with no Route B selection and different owners. I had verified that scope in earlier cycles and did not apply it here, because the attack I was testing was whether the coordinator pretended to be the owner, the entry disclaimed that in four places, and I stopped at the disclaimer instead of following the pointer. The repair is better than a withdrawal: it records the owner path as blocked, names the two things that would unblock it, and separates owner-recording from the MF-6 that must follow it. What remains is one note about a disclosure that went missing in the rewrite — that Codex filed no turn-1 verdict — which is still inferable from the pins table but was worth keeping in words.
